items.definition: The roughly 24-hour cycle that sets your sleep, hormones, body temperature and appetite. Light is its strongest input.
items.example: My circadian rhythm has shifted, because I have been going to bed at two every night.

items.definition: The time between getting into bed and falling asleep. Under about twenty minutes is normal.
items.example: My sleep onset latency is about forty minutes, most nights.

items.definition: The share of your time in bed that you were actually asleep. A long night can still be an inefficient one.
items.example: I was in bed for nine hours and my sleep efficiency was about seventy per cent.

items.definition: The accumulated gap between the sleep you have had and the sleep you need. It can be partly repaid, but slowly.
items.example: I have been building up sleep debt for three weeks of early starts.

items.definition: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early, together with daytime impairment. The daytime effect is part of the definition.
items.example: It is not just that I sleep badly; it is that I cannot work properly the next day. That makes it insomnia.

items.definition: Repeated pauses in breathing during sleep, usually with snoring and gasping. You usually cannot notice it yourself.
items.example: My partner says I stop breathing in my sleep, so I will ask about sleep apnoea.

items.definition: Something you notice and describe yourself: pain, dizziness, a cough, a lump.
items.example: The main symptom is the pain, and it has been there for three weeks.

items.definition: A written symbol such as = or +.
items.example: The equals sign balances both sides.

items.definition: Coming on quickly and lasting a short time, usually days.
items.example: This is an acute episode, and it started yesterday.

items.definition: Long-standing, generally present for more than three months.
items.example: It has become a chronic problem, so I have started to manage it differently.

items.definition: A period when the symptoms get noticeably worse than their usual level.
items.example: The main exacerbation lasted about four days last month.

items.definition: The clinician's shortlist of possible causes, kept in mind while they examine you and order tests.
items.example: The doctor said the differential included three possibilities, and explained each one.

items.definition: A letter sending you to another service, such as a specialist, a physiotherapist or a scan.
items.example: I have a referral for a scan, and the appointment is in ten days.

items.definition: A machine with two wheels that you push with your feet. A good bicycle makes your legs feel like they have a strong friend.
items.example: His grandfather's bicycle was heavy and rusty, and Nam loved it.

items.definition: The flat part of a bicycle that your foot stands on. When you push the pedals, the wheels turn.
items.example: The pedals were stiff, so he pushed them three times.

items.definition: The flat part that helps a bird to lift into the air. On this bicycle, the wings are only paper, but they still lift.
items.example: The newspaper wings lifted when he rang the bell.

items.definition: The small metal thing on a bicycle that makes a sound when you press it. Nam's bell is old and a bit tired.
items.example: He pressed the bell three times before the wings moved.

items.definition: The flat top of a building. In the old quarter, the rooftops are close enough to almost touch.
items.example: They landed on the roof garden above the old house.

items.definition: A big old building with thick walls, made to keep people safe. Castles usually have towers and gates.
items.example: From her window, Hà could see the castle on the hill.

items.definition: A tall round part of a castle. You can climb to the top of a tower and look out over everything.
items.example: The castle had one round tower with a flag on top.

items.definition: A small metal thing that opens a lock. A keyhole is the hole where the key goes in.
items.example: The small brass key hung on a red string.

items.definition: A piece of ground where people grow plants and flowers. A garden needs water and a little care every day.
items.example: The green door opened on a garden under a round moon.

items.definition: An animal that lived a very long time ago, long before people. Dinosaurs are gone now, but their bones turn to stone under the ground.
items.example: The long-necked dinosaur pulled leaves from the treetop.

items.definition: The hard part of an animal that turned to stone after a very long time. Fossils tell us what the animal looked like.
items.example: She found a yellow fossil under a huge leaf.

items.definition: The mark a foot leaves in soft ground. Big animals leave big footprints, and they show which way the animal walked.
items.example: The footprints pointed deeper into the valley.

items.definition: An animal that eats plants, such as a zebra, a giraffe or an elephant.
items.example: The elephant is a herbivore, so it eats grass and leaves.

items.definition: An animal that eats other animals. Carnivores are often the strong, heavy ones.
items.example: The heavy animal with the thick tail was a carnivore.

items.definition: A green climbing plant that grows up walls and trees. It holds on tightly and hides what is behind it.
items.example: Ivy grew across the green door.

items.definition: An open space in the middle of woods, where the trees step back and the sky reaches the ground.
items.example: The path led to a small clearing.

items.definition: To put a seed into the ground and look after it. Planting is a promise to come back.
items.example: Bình planted the seed on the first of April.

items.definition: Kept out of sight, so that people walk past without noticing.
items.example: The door was hidden under the ivy.

items.definition: Something you want very much and keep safe. It can be gold, but it can also be a letter or a photograph.
items.example: The box in the grass held the real treasure.

items.definition: A drawing of a place, seen from above. A map shows you the way and shows you where things are.
items.example: Tuấn unfolded the old map on the kitchen table.

items.definition: A small hint. Clues come one after another, and each one points to the next.
items.example: The third clue was a picture of a bench and a nail.

items.definition: A small tool with a needle that points north. Explorers use a compass so they walk in a straight line.
items.example: The compass needle spun because of the iron in the ground.

items.definition: A small mountain, high in the middle and low at the edges. You can walk up a hill in a few minutes.
items.example: They walked up the hill to look for the treasure.

items.definition: A machine that pushes itself up into the sky with fire and gas. It is how people reach space.
items.example: The rocket stood on the pad, white and tall.

items.definition: The platform where the rocket stands and waits before it flies.
items.example: Everybody watched from the launch pad.

items.definition: A person trained to fly into space. Astronauts wear a spacesuit because there is no air out there.
items.example: The astronaut opened the hatch and stepped out.

items.definition: The feeling of floating, with nothing pulling you down. Everything drifts in the ship.
items.example: In weightlessness, even a pencil can float.
